panels.description: Wide, full page width. Dawn. A narrow strip of Malabar beach pinned between a low laterite bluff crowned with coconut palms and the Arabian Sea. Low tide: a broad plain of packed wet sand shining like beaten tin. The sun has only just cleared the palms. Far down the beach, small, the Madurai troop rides toward us, dressed as Carnatic cavalry of the 1740s: knee-length white jama tunics with plain cloth waistbands, loose trousers, high-wrapped white or off-white turbans (never green, red or rust), quilted Indian saddles, long bamboo lances with no pennons, no European uniform elements. Tall, heavy horses in dark bay, dark brown and black, no greys. One deep-green turban at the head of the column.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The first time I tried to make Madurai horses run in Malabar sand, they laughed at me.

panels.description: Tight and low, at hoof level. A heavy dark-bay horse's foreleg planted at the wet margin, the hoof sunk to the pastern, grey slurry welling around it, a thin sheet of foam sliding in.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Not with their mouths. Horses do not waste breath on that.

panels.description: Tight on the same dark-bay horse's eye, rolling, the white showing, turned toward us. A real horse's eye, no human expression, no grin. Above it, out of focus, the edge of a white turban and a lance shaft.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Every rolling eye said what the riders did not dare speak aloud.

copy.speaker: CAPTION (italic, the words no rider spoke)
copy.text: You do not belong here, Deccan man.

panels.description: Medium. The troop has arrived. At its head, Raza Khan: lean, hawk nose, pointed moustache, a puckered scar on his ANATOMICAL LEFT cheek (our right as he faces us), deep-green high-wrapped turban, the only green turban on the beach, white jama, on a tall, heavy dark-bay horse. He salutes with his spear butt to his chest. Behind him the Madurai riders sit straight in white jamas and white turbans, bamboo lances gleaming with no pennons, their dark horses tossing their heads.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: His Hindustani carried the singsong of the Carnatic.

copy.speaker: RAZA KHAN
copy.text: Raza Khan, at your service. The Nayak of Madurai sends his horse as promised.

copy.speaker: RAZA KHAN
copy.text: We have fought for Madurai and for your king before.

panels.description: Reverse angle. Nagoji, mounted on a plain grey, first full view of the commander look, drawn from the full-length commander figure on the Nagoji sheet and not its bare-headed face studies: rust-red turban with his long curly hair gathered beneath it and curls showing at the nape, cream tunic, broad red sash knotted at the waist, cream trousers, boots, talwar at his hip. Thick curled moustache, CLEAN-SHAVEN CHIN, small gold ear stud. He is not looking at us. He is weighing them.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Too confident.

panels.description: Low angle up at the bluff. A line of Maravar horsemen on small, rough-coated ponies in dun and dark brown (no greys) that shift and stamp. No uniforms: bare-headed, plain white or undyed mundus hitched for riding, short jackets, swords worn as if they were born wearing them. Only Ponnan wears red. At their front, Ponnan: BARE-HEADED, short curly hair, broader and stockier than Nagoji, thick moustache, clean chin, short dark-brown jacket, a narrow red cloth over his right shoulder, white mundu hitched to the knee, bare legs, on a small rough-coated dun pony.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Ponnam Pandya Deven. Ponnan to his riders.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: He had already ridden the inland tracks with me. He said little. His eyes missed nothing.

panels.description: Long shot through heat haze rising off the sand. On the lower shoulder of the bluff, above the sand and a little along from the Maravar line, a one-pole cloth awning, and under it two small figures on low stools. Marthanda Varma: take ONLY the face and moustache from the varma-v1 sheet and ignore its headwear; NO turban, NO peacock crest; black hair tied in a bun to his left; simple Vaishnavite lines on the forehead; bare-chested, a single cream-and-gold cloth over one shoulder, gold necklaces; his spear leaning against the awning pole. Beside him Ramayyan: thin, sharp fine features, receding hair, plain white cloth, a bundle of palm leaves in his lap and the stylus ready.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Marthanda Varma had told me, in that coastal hall, to show him something he had not already imagined.

panels.description: Insert, tight. Nagoji's LEFT hand on the reins of the grey, the cream sleeve pushed back toward the elbow, the nails healed but ridged. On the inner side of the left forearm, a hand's width above the wrist, the Portuguese brand: a short row of raised, ridged burn scars, healed now to pale puckered skin, crude marks blurred past reading. No legible letters, no numerals, no cross.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: At the time, with the memory of chains still raw on my skin, the challenge had felt almost like grace.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Now it sat on me like a weight.

panels.description: On the sand, three riders abreast, facing down the beach. Left to right: Raza Khan (deep-green turban, scar on his anatomical left cheek, pointed moustache, white jama, on a tall, heavy dark-bay horse); Nagoji in the centre, pointing down the beach to the waterline with his right arm (rust-red turban, clean-shaven chin, thick curled moustache, cream tunic, red sash, boots, on the tall grey); Ponnan on the right (bare-headed, short curly hair, dark-brown jacket, red cloth over his right shoulder, white mundu, bare legs, on a small dun pony, noticeably lower than the other two).

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: We begin with the simple release. Ride to the water's edge. Turn. Ride back.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Do not let the hoof slide.

panels.description: Raza Khan, frowning, one hand resting on his pommel, his left cheek toward us so the scar reads. Deep-green high-wrapped turban, pointed moustache, white jama, on his dark-bay horse.

copy.speaker: RAZA KHAN
copy.text: We did not ride from Madurai to school our mounts like children on their first pony.

copy.speaker: RAZA KHAN
copy.text: My men ride to break lines, not to dance with crabs.

panels.description: Nagoji on the grey, level, the sea bright behind him. Rust-red turban with curls at the nape below it, clean-shaven chin, thick curled moustache, small gold ear stud, cream tunic, red sash.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Your men ride on hard earth. Here the ground lies to you. It looks firm, but it drinks the hoof.

panels.description: Tight on Raza Khan, his left cheek toward the camera so the scar reads; deep-green high-wrapped turban, pointed moustache. His jaw tightens. His eyes flick UP and away. Above and behind his shoulder, small and hazy on the shoulder of the bluff, the one-pole awning where the king sits.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI (off)
copy.text: If you charge a Dutch square and your horse stumbles on the turn, you are not a soldier, you are a target.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The king had set a stranger over him.

panels.description: Raza Khan (deep-green turban, white jama) wheeling his dark-bay horse away, calling back over his shoulder. Inset, upper corner: Ponnan (bare-headed, short curly hair, red cloth over his right shoulder, dark-brown jacket), a faint smile at the corner of his mouth, lifting one hand to signal his Maravar on the bluff.

copy.speaker: RAZA KHAN
copy.text: One pass. To show you there is no magic in sand.

panels.description: Wide, half the page, generated at its placed aspect ratio. The Madurai line thunders toward the waterline in full pride: white jamas, white and off-white turbans, bamboo lances high with no pennons, spray flying, every dark horse in stride. Raza Khan's single deep-green turban at the front. Behind them the Maravar, bare-headed on dun and dark-brown ponies, stream down the face of the bluff to follow. It looks magnificent.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The first pass was a disaster.

panels.description: Large, the top half of the page, generated at its placed aspect ratio. The turn at the water's edge. The heavy Madurai horses (dark bay, dark brown, black) sink as they try to turn: hooves sucked into the slurry, legs flailing for footing, a bamboo lance tipping sideways, riders in white jamas and white turbans hauling on the reins to keep their seats. Raza Khan's deep-green turban is caught in the middle of it. The proud line has become a knot. At the right edge of the same frame, a few lengths clear, a Maravar dun pony that also slipped on the turn: it has thrown a fan of wet sand, but it has already found its feet and is darting away across the surface while the big horses bog down. Its bare-headed rider in white grins back over his shoulder at the floundering southerners.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Bred for the dry country around Madurai.

panels.description: Nagoji riding his grey between the two lines, one arm out, calling to both. Rust-red turban, clean-shaven chin, thick curled moustache, cream tunic, red sash, boots.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: See? The earth here judges weight. It punishes force.

panels.description: Two riders abreast as the line wheels back toward firmer ground. Nearer the camera, Nagoji on the tall grey (rust-red turban, cream tunic, red sash, cream trousers, boots). Beyond him, a head lower, Ponnan on his small dun pony (BARE-HEADED, short curly hair, broader and stockier, dark-brown jacket, red cloth over his right shoulder, white mundu, bare legs). Ponnan speaks quietly, eyes forward, not turning his head.

copy.speaker: PONNAN
copy.text: This earth has judged hooves longer than you have ridden, Deccan man.

copy.speaker: PONNAN
copy.text: We learned that under other kings.

panels.description: Two-shot, riding side by side. Nagoji on the tall grey (rust-red turban, clean-shaven chin, thick curled moustache, cream tunic, red sash, boots) and Ponnan on his small dun pony, a head lower (bare-headed, short curly hair, dark-brown jacket, red cloth over his right shoulder, white mundu, bare legs). In the background, small, Raza Khan in his deep-green turban cursing at his dark-bay horse. Ponnan's eyes have slid toward him.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Then teach your Madurai friends. Today they followed me into the bog. Tomorrow they follow you around it.

copy.speaker: PONNAN
copy.text: We will see whose tricks the Dutch remember.

panels.description: Raza Khan, still mounted, his dark-bay horse back on firm ground. Furious, he shakes his boot in the stirrup and clods of wet sand fall from it. Deep-green turban, scar on his anatomical left cheek, pointed moustache, white jama.

copy.speaker: RAZA KHAN
copy.text: It is a bog. No cavalry can fight here.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI (off)
copy.text: The Dutch will be here. If you cannot fight where they stand, why did you take the king's coin?

panels.description: Raza Khan, still mounted, his left cheek toward the camera so the scar reads, deep-green turban, pointed moustache, glaring down at Nagoji off panel. But his eyes drop, for a moment, to his horse's sand-caked legs. The anger is already cooling into shame. Nagoji's balloons come from off panel.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI (off)
copy.text: Again. But this time, do not fight the ground.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI (off)
copy.text: Let the horse find the bottom before you ask for the turn. You must ride with the sand, not against it.

panels.description: Wide, later. Heat shimmer. The bamboo lances stand stacked upright in the sand, no pennons, no formation. The riders work in a mixed line along the water's edge: one heavy dark Madurai horse with a white-turbaned rider, then one light dun Maravar pony with a bare-headed rider, then another pair, making slow turns in the slurry. Men soaked in sweat.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: We spent the morning in that slurry.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The Malabar coast did not care about their lineage.

panels.description: Water pause, midday, the air rippling. Raza Khan drinking from a gourd, sweat-soaked, his deep-green turban loosened a little, the scar on his anatomical left cheek showing, pointed moustache. Nagoji beside him, squatting on his heels: rust-red turban, clean-shaven chin, thick curled moustache, cream tunic, red sash, boots.

copy.speaker: RAZA KHAN
copy.text: This is not war. This is labour.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: It is the only war that matters today.

panels.description: Nagoji talking, still on his heels: rust-red turban, clean-shaven chin, thick curled moustache, gold ear stud, cream tunic, red sash. Behind him, out on the flat, a long wave slides in at a slant across the sand, fast and sideways.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: The Dutch carry muskets that fire in volleys. Precise. Mechanical. If you charge them straight, they will break you.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: You must come at them like the tide. Fast, from the angle they do not expect, and gone before they can reload.

panels.description: Raza Khan wiping his face with the tail of his deep-green turban cloth, his left cheek and its scar toward us, pointed moustache. In the foreground, Nagoji's hand, cream sleeve, closing on a piece of driftwood.

copy.speaker: RAZA KHAN
copy.text: To ride like the tide, one must first not drown in the sand.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI (off)
copy.text: Exactly.

panels.description: Inset, square, straight down from overhead. The driftwood tip scoring one straight groove in the wet sand. Grooves in wet sand only, made by the driftwood tip; no arrows, symbols, letters or labels. It sits at the left of the upper band of 6.5.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI (off)
copy.text: The Dutch line.

panels.description: Inset, square, the same overhead angle. The straight groove, and two curved grooves sweeping in from either flank, bending toward it and hooking away before they touch it. Grooves in wet sand only, made by the driftwood tip; no arrows, symbols, letters or labels. It sits at the right of the upper band of 6.5, beside 6.3.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI (off)
copy.text: Us. We do not hit them. We bait them.

panels.description: Large, the lower half of the page, full width at ground level, generated at its placed aspect ratio. Keep the upper third as open sea and sky, clear for the two insets. The drawing in the foreground. Behind it, Nagoji (rust-red turban, clean-shaven chin, thick curled moustache, cream tunic, red sash) and Raza Khan (deep-green turban, scar on his anatomical left cheek toward us, pointed moustache, white jama) crouched over it. A thin sheet of foam has slid in and is softening the end of the Dutch line.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: We ride close, close enough to make them level their muskets. Then we turn.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: If we slip then, we die.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: If we turn true, they fire at ghosts, and while they reload, we take them with the sabre.

panels.description: Raza Khan still crouched, studying the half-erased map: deep-green turban, scar on his anatomical left cheek toward us, pointed moustache, white jama. Across from him, Nagoji (rust-red turban, clean-shaven chin, thick curled moustache, cream tunic, red sash), forearms on his knees.

copy.speaker: RAZA KHAN
copy.text: It is a gamble. To ride into the teeth of the gun and turn away.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: It is better than riding into the teeth and staying there.

panels.description: Raza Khan rising, looking out at the horses: deep-green turban, pointed moustache, scar on his anatomical left cheek. A small balloon, almost to himself. Nagoji (rust-red turban, cream tunic, red sash, boots) already walking back toward his grey.

copy.speaker: RAZA KHAN (small)
copy.text: If the horses hold.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Make them hold.

panels.description: Wide, half the page, generated at its placed aspect ratio. Afternoon, the sun lower, the tide higher. The mixed line (white-turbaned Madurai riders on dark horses, bare-headed Maravar on dun ponies, alternating) wheels together at the water's edge in one clean turn, a single arc of thrown spray behind it. The heavy horses give to the sand instead of fighting it. The riders sit quiet in the saddle. Nobody is hauling on a rein.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Men began to trust that their mounts would not vanish under them at every turn.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Horses began to trust that their riders would not ask for impossible strides.

panels.description: The top of the bluff, at the one-pole awning. Marthanda Varma has risen from his stool and stands at the awning's edge: ONLY the face and moustache from the varma-v1 sheet, NO turban, NO peacock crest, black hair tied in a bun to his left, simple Vaishnavite lines on the forehead, bare-chested, a single cream-and-gold cloth over one shoulder, gold necklaces. Ramayyan (thin, sharp fine features, receding hair, plain white cloth) on his stool, writing a last mark on a palm leaf. Nagoji has just ridden up the slope and is swinging down from the grey: rust-red turban, clean-shaven chin, thick curled moustache, cream tunic, red sash, sweat drying on his skin, wet sand caked on his boots and trouser legs.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: You make them move like fish. Not like bulls.

panels.description: Nagoji, reins in hand, the grey's head at his shoulder, answering the king at a respectful distance. Rust-red turban with curls at the nape below it, clean-shaven chin, thick curled moustache, small gold ear stud, cream tunic, red sash.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Fish do not charge muskets. But yes.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: If your enemies expect bulls, better to be something else.

panels.description: High wide shot over Marthanda Varma's shoulder, from behind at three-quarter: bare head with black hair tied in a bun to his left, NO turban, NO peacock crest, a cream-and-gold cloth over one bare shoulder, the edge of a gold necklace. He nods slowly. Below, down the slope, the mixed Madurai and Maravar line regroups on the shining sand, tiny figures in white turbans and bare heads against the bright strip of water.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: They are not yet ready. But they are less foolish than they were at sunrise.

panels.description: Ramayyan (thin, sharp fine features, receding hair, plain white cloth) looking up from his palm leaves at Nagoji. Nagoji (rust-red turban, clean-shaven chin, thick curled moustache, gold ear stud, cream tunic) turning to him.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: They obeyed you. Even when their pride bucked harder than their horses.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: They obeyed the king's order. I am only the voice today.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: Voices matter. Especially when the sea is loud.

panels.description: Wide. The open sea from the bluff, a line of darker blue on the horizon marking deep water. No ships. Marthanda Varma small at the awning's edge, in silhouette against the bright sky: the bun of hair to his left and the cloth over one shoulder readable in outline, NO turban, NO crest, the spear in his hand.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: The Dutch think these sands belong to them.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: They think their boots and bayonets make them owners.

panels.description: Tight on Marthanda Varma as he turns his head and looks at Nagoji (off panel) directly. ONLY the face and moustache from the varma-v1 sheet, NO turban, NO peacock crest: black hair tied in a bun to his left, simple Vaishnavite lines on the forehead, gold necklaces at the bottom of the frame. Nothing else in the frame matters.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: Show me, Nagoji Sawant, that horses can disagree.

panels.description: Nagoji bows his head, once. Rust-red turban with curls at the nape below it, clean-shaven chin, thick curled moustache, small gold ear stud, cream tunic, red sash.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: I will try.

panels.description: Wide. Nagoji on the grey riding back down the slope (rust-red turban, cream tunic, red sash, cream trousers, boots) toward the strip of wet sand, where the Madurai and Maravar riders wait together now, white turbans and bare heads mixed, catching their breath, their horses side by side. The tide is coming in.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Fear, yes. Responsibility, sharp as any spear point.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: But also something I had not felt since before Goa, before the dungeon, before the storm.

panels.description: Narrow strip. Nagoji's eyes, forward. The strip runs from the lower edge of the rust-red turban down to the top of the thick curled moustache; keep the turban's edge inside the frame. Take the face from the sheet's commander figure, not its bare-headed studies.

copy.speaker: CAPTION (separate, weighted)
copy.text: Anticipation.

panels.description: Wide. Dusk. The picket line under the palms, horses rubbed down, cook fires scattered in the dark beyond. Nagoji walking alone among the mounts: rust-red turban, cream tunic, red sash, cream trousers, boots. Bleeding into the panel's edge like a stain rather than a clean flashback frame, the same device as Chapter 1, panel 6.5: a black mare at full stretch across black Deccan soil, alive, with no rider and no saddle, mane and tail streaming.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: In the Deccan I had ridden Kanka, a black mare with a temper like monsoon lightning.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: She died at Vasai, a Portuguese ball through her chest. I walked the last miles to Goa too stunned to mourn properly.

panels.description: At the far end of the picket line, apart from the others: Kayal, a bay mare, ochre red-brown body with BLACK mane, tail and lower legs, no white markings on face or legs, fine head, compact frame, a little taller than the Maravar ponies and clearly smaller than the Madurai horses. No other red-bay horse near her. Ears forward, head a little high. She is watching him come.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Neither Madurai nor Maravar. Something in between.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: I knew that look. Wariness. Interest. The calculation of a creature deciding whether to trust.

panels.description: Nagoji walking toward her down the line (rust-red turban, cream tunic, red sash, boots), past small rough-coated Maravar ponies in dun and dark brown with watchful eyes, and taller, elegant Madurai horses in dark bay, dark brown and black, shifting uneasily in the damp. At the end of the line, Kayal: bay, ochre red-brown coat, black mane, tail and lower legs, no white markings. No other red-bay horse near her.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Every war horse on this coast was an import, and every one cost more than a soldier's yearly wage.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: But the Maravar ponies knew the monsoon in their bones.

panels.description: Nagoji holding out his hand, palm up and low: rust-red turban with curls at the nape below it, clean-shaven chin, thick curled moustache, gold ear stud. Kayal (bay, ochre red-brown coat, black mane, no white markings) stretches her neck toward his hand, nostrils flared, taking his scent.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: You do not belong to any of them either. Do you?

panels.description: Kayal pushes her nose into Nagoji's chest. His hand has come to rest on her neck, under the black mane. His eyes are closed. Nagoji: rust-red turban, curls at the nape, clean-shaven chin, thick curled moustache, cream tunic.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: It was not Kanka's smell. It never would be.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: But it was honest.

panels.description: Close two-shot, his forehead near her face, the last light on her ochre red-brown coat and black forelock. Nagoji: rust-red turban edge in frame, curls at the nape, clean-shaven chin, thick curled moustache, small gold ear stud; take the face from the sheet's commander figure, not its bare-headed studies. Kayal: no white markings on her face.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Kayal.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The word came unbidden. The Malayalam name for the backwaters.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: You will learn the sand with me. And when the Dutch come, we will show them what a backwater horse can do.

panels.description: Kayal tosses her head, black mane flying, as if agreeing to terms she has not yet heard. Nagoji almost smiles: rust-red turban, clean-shaven chin, thick curled moustache, cream tunic, red sash.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: It was the first time since Vasai that I had named a horse.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The first time I had let myself care whether one particular animal lived or died.

panels.description: Wide, full page width. The last light going blue over the picket line, the palms, and the sea beyond. Small in a large, quiet frame, Nagoji stands alone with Kayal at the end of the line, his hand on her neck. Nagoji: rust-red turban, cream tunic, red sash, cream trousers, boots. Kayal: bay, ochre red-brown coat, black mane, tail and lower legs.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Kayal would carry me through Colachel and beyond.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: But that night, all I knew was the strange comfort of belonging, even a little, to this unfamiliar land.

panels.description: Evening shadow. Ibrahim Marakkar leaning against a palm trunk nearby: shorter than Nagoji but broader, white turban, short grey-flecked beard, short coat over a vest with bulging pockets, white mundu; no green, no hawk nose. His right side is in shadow and his anatomical LEFT side is lit, so the scar from his left ear to the corner of his jaw reads. Nagoji (rust-red turban, clean-shaven chin, thick curled moustache, cream tunic) with his hand still on Kayal's neck.

copy.speaker: IBRAHIM
copy.text: You talk to horses. I have seen men talk to worse.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Horses do not argue. They simply refuse, or they follow. It is simpler than men.

panels.description: Ibrahim, arms folded, studying him: white turban, short grey-flecked beard, the scar from his LEFT ear to his jaw lit, short coat over a vest with bulging pockets.

copy.speaker: IBRAHIM
copy.text: You are Hindu.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: After a fashion. The Portuguese tried to convince me otherwise. It did not take.

copy.speaker: IBRAHIM
copy.text: And yet I have seen you bow your head in their churches.

panels.description: Nagoji with a half-shrug, one hand still on Kayal's black mane: rust-red turban with curls at the nape, clean-shaven chin, thick curled moustache, small gold ear stud, cream tunic, red sash.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: I pray to whatever is listening. If the gods are as numerous as men say, surely one of them has time for a cavalryman with sand in his boots.

panels.description: Ibrahim, quiet for a moment, his eyes going past Nagoji toward the dark water. White turban, short grey-flecked beard, his anatomical left side lit so the scar reads, short coat over the vest.

copy.speaker: IBRAHIM
copy.text: I am Muslim. My fathers came from the coast of Arabia, traders who married local women and stayed.

panels.description: Ibrahim half turned toward the sea, one hand flat on the palm trunk: white turban, short grey-flecked beard, scar from his LEFT ear to his jaw, short coat over a vest with bulging pockets. Nagoji (rust-red turban, clean-shaven chin, thick curled moustache, cream tunic) listening beside Kayal (bay, black mane).

copy.speaker: IBRAHIM
copy.text: We built mosques. We kept the faith. But we also lit lamps at Hindu shrines when our ships sailed, and we asked Christian priests to bless our cargo when the winds were wrong.

panels.description: Wide. Dusk beyond the palms: the sea and the mouth of a backwater channel meeting, pale salt surf folding into dark, still channel water. Ibrahim (white turban), Nagoji (rust-red turban) and Kayal small at the edge of the frame.

copy.speaker: IBRAHIM
copy.text: On this coast, the gods mix like the waters of the backwaters, salt and fresh, never quite one thing. A man who insists on purity drowns faster than one who learns to float in both.

panels.description: Ibrahim pushing off from the palm, facing Nagoji: white turban, short grey-flecked beard, his anatomical left side toward us so the scar reads, short coat over a vest with bulging pockets. Nagoji's rust-red turban and shoulder at the edge of frame.

copy.speaker: IBRAHIM
copy.text: You are useful too, Sawant. That is why you are still alive.

copy.speaker: IBRAHIM
copy.text: The king does not keep men for their faith. He keeps them for what they can do.

panels.description: Ibrahim walking away into the gathering dark, speaking over his shoulder, his white turban catching the last light. In the foreground, Nagoji (rust-red turban, cream tunic, red sash) and Kayal watching him go.

copy.speaker: IBRAHIM
copy.text: Remember that, when you wonder why a Muslim sailor and a Hindu horseman and a Christian merchant all sit in the same war hall.

panels.description: Full width, bottom, the largest panel on the page, generated at its placed aspect ratio. Night. Nagoji alone with Kayal at the edge of the wet sand, the sea a pale line behind them. Nagoji: rust-red turban, cream tunic, red sash, cream trousers, boots. Kayal: bay, black mane and tail, no white markings. At their feet, the day's hoofprints are filling with water.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: On Deccan soil, I had thought I knew the limits of what a horse could do against a gun. Here, those limits shifted.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Storms did not ask permission.

copy.speaker: CAPTION (separate, weighted)
copy.text: Perhaps horses, taught well, did not either.
